fields.note: 2 October 2026: replaces save this script as. Save As copied the open file, so the new file declared the old class_name until its code was typed (Godot: 'Class Field hides a global script class'), and typing the new code into the old file first let a run save over it. A new script starts empty of classes: Godot fills it with its own few lines, which the last step replaces. The file's name follows the call in code style: 'Make a new script `bell.gd`.' The script is then put on the top node by put a script on a node (1.3), or, for a class (4.7, 4.8), made with .new(). 4.7 is its first need: spray_can.gd, the first script that is not the top node's (moved from 18.1 by the chapter 4 writer, as this note foresaw); 18.1 calls it. Save As wordings ('Save the file as `bell2.gd`') describe getting a script under a new name, so they are its synonyms and step phrases: say 'Make a new script'. File is the menu of the Script screen (the Script button at the top); 'Choose Save As to keep the old scene' is no step of this (the cues: script, File, .gd). The editor steps (Script, File, New Script, the name, Create) are NOT verified in a live editor: the checker cannot click.

why: 4.7 makes spray_can.gd, the first second script in the book; the definition moves there and 18.1's bold definition becomes the call 'Make a new script `field.gd`.' (ch18.md must change with this patch)
